reasoning: The failure-driven option-audit rule takes priority over the overlapping success-driven equivalence and qualifier checks. The success-driven estimate and symbolic-verification procedures add distinct guidance, so they are retained. All edits append outside the protected section.

edits.content: For “strongest valid” and equivalence questions, split each option into separate claims and verify every clause independently. One unsupported modifier invalidates the option; equivalence requires both implications under the stated hypotheses.
For quantitative estimates, check the domain of each norm and the stated dependencies of constants literally; local and global bounds are not interchangeable.

For a long symbolic identity, verify specialized calculations term by term, including coefficients and constant terms, before treating an apparent contradiction as decisive. In a quotient ring, compare expressions modulo the defining relation; evaluations can disprove an identity but do not establish it.
